chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Convey my greetings upon those of them whom you see obeying me and following my words. And I advise you all with the fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and devoutness in your religion, and striving for God, and truthfulness of speech, and fulfilling trusts, and prolonging prostration, and good neighbourliness. For it is by this that Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) came.

Fulfil the trust to whoever entrusted you with it, whether he be righteous or wicked, for the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to command the return of even the thread and the needle. Maintain ties with your kin, attend their funerals, console their sick, and fulfil their rights.

For when a man from you is devout in his religion, truthful in speech, fulfils trusts, and is of good character with people, it is said: This is a Ja'fari — and that gladdens me, and joy enters upon me from it, and it is said: This is the teaching of Ja'far. But when he is otherwise, its suffering and its disgrace come upon me, and it is said: This is the teaching of Ja'far.

By God, my father (peace be upon him) told me that there used to be a man in a tribe from the Shias of Ali (peace be upon him), and he was its ornament — the most faithful of them in trusts, the most fulfilling of them in rights, and the most truthful of them in speech. Their wills and deposits were left with him. The tribe was asked about him, and they would say: Who is like so-and-so? He is the most faithful of us in trusts and the most truthful of us in speech.

key_terms.أدب جعفر: The adab (teaching/training) of Ja'far — the Imam's character and school of virtue, by which followers are judged
key_terms.الأمانة: Amanah — trust, entrustment; the obligation to return what is entrusted, regardless of the trustor's character
key_terms.الاجتهاد: Striving, diligence in worship and religious duty; here used in the sense of effort for God's sake
key_terms.الورع: Wara' — scrupulous piety, avoidance of doubtful matters; higher standard than mere compliance
key_terms.جعفري: A Ja'fari — one who belongs to and exemplifies the school of Imam al-Sadiq (AS)

ai.seo_question: What qualities did Imam al-Sadiq say define a true Ja'fari Shia?
ai.summary: In this comprehensive exhortation, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) charges Zayd al-Shahham to convey his greetings to his true followers and then delivers a sweeping moral program centered on seven virtues: taqwa (God-consciousness), religious scrupulosity (wara'), striving for God, truthfulness in speech, fulfilling trusts, prolonged prostration, and good neighbourliness. He grounds these in the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), making clear these are not mere recommendations but the very substance of prophetic teaching. The Imam concludes with a powerful reminder that a Shia's reputation — whether praise or reproach — reflects directly upon the Imam himself, thus making ethical conduct a communal responsibility that affects the honour of the Imamate.
